source.title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications

accepted.question_text: Given a relativistic quantum field theory that flows under the renormalization group from a ultraviolet conformal field theory to an infrared endpoint, is there a general principle that determines which conformal RG domain wall or conformal boundary state is selected from the possible boundary states connecting those ultraviolet and infrared theories?
accepted.context_brief: RG domain walls and boundary states

evidence.quote: Are there general principles that select the RG domain wall(s)/boundary state(s) from the possible set connecting the UV and IR endpoints of RG ﬂows?

accepted.question_text: How much additional structure can supersymmetry reveal about boundary conformal field theories and defect conformal field theories, in particular through tools such as supersymmetric localization?

evidence.quote: What more can SUSY tell us about bCFTs and dCFTs, for example via SUSY localization?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist boundary or defect monotonicity theorems in dimensions higher than two that generalize the two-dimensional g-theorem for boundary conformal field theory?

evidence.quote: Are there boundary or defect “ c-theorems" generalizing the g-theorem [208,209] of two-dimensional bCFT to higher dimensions?

accepted.question_text: Can techniques such as supersymmetry, the conformal bootstrap, integrability, and topological field theory be pushed far enough to discover genuinely new conformal boundary conditions, new conformal defects, or even new conceptual formulations of quantum field theory?
accepted.context_brief: Methods for new defects and QFT viewpoints

evidence.quote: Could they also lead to the discovery of new conformal boundary conditions, defects, or even entirely new perspectives on what QFT is?

accepted.question_text: Can the boundary- and defect-conformal-field-theory methods used to diagnose and characterize topological phases in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions be generalized to a higher-dimensional analogue, especially for higher-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to explore if there is a higher dimensional analogue of the approaches discussed in this article.

accepted.question_text: For classical sine-Gordon scattering on a half-line with integrability broken at the boundary, how can one completely reconstruct the outgoing soliton content of the final state, including breathers and any additional kink-antikink pairs rather than only the net topological charge, and what dynamical mechanism produces the intricate almost fractal structures seen in the phase diagram of boundary scattering outcomes?

evidence.quote: At this stage there are two immediate questions: ﬁrst, how can we disentangle the full soliton content of the ﬁnal state? So far we only looked at the net topological charge, but this is blind both to breathers and to additional kink-antikink pairs. Second, what’s going on? What is the reason for the complicated, almost fractal, structures present in some parts of ﬁgure 6?

accepted.question_text: For the tricritical Ising model, can one construct exact non-topological, non-factorizing conformal defects, including an explicit partition function for the proposed defects despite the breaking of superconformal symmetry by the interface operators, and can one derive the relevant boundary conditions from first principles rather than only by indirect constructions?
accepted.context_brief: Defects in the tricritical Ising model

evidence.quote: the challenge is to ﬁnd non-topological non-factorising conformal defects.
We have not been able to ﬁnd the partition function owing the breaking of superconformal symmetry by the Interface operators.
It would be interesting to derive the boundary conditions for the free fermion and SVIR3 from ﬁrst principles or using the methods of Novak and Runkel [84].

accepted.question_text: In the defect conformal field theory associated with the D3-D5 brane system, can one obtain enough control of the three-dimensional theory living on the defect to fully exploit boundary conformal bootstrap equations based on one- and two-point functions, and can one derive a closed formula for tree-level one-point functions in the closely related SO(5)-symmetric D3-D7 defect conformal field theory where the full scalar SO(6) sector contributes?
accepted.context_brief: Bootstrap and one-point functions in dCFT

evidence.quote: Taking it further would potentially be very interesting but in order to fully exploit it for the present dCFT a better understanding of the 3D theory living on the defect is needed.

As regards the integrability properties of one-point functions an interesting question is whether a closed formula can be found even at tree-level for the closely related SO(5) symmetric D3-D7-brane based dCFT.

accepted.question_text: Can one perform a string-theoretic computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator in the AdS/dCFT setting, beyond the cases of chiral primary operators where closed expressions are already known?

evidence.quote: Finally, an open problem is to perform a string theoretical computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator.

accepted.question_text: For four-point correlators of chiral primary operators in N = 4 super Yang-Mills at large 't Hooft coupling, how should one incorporate 1/λ corrections, how can one include the exchange of finitely many single-trace operators at order 1/N^4, and how can bootstrap-based calculations be combined consistently with direct one-loop Witten-diagram computations and integrability-based methods?
accepted.context_brief: Loop corrections in AdS5 x S5

evidence.quote: There are open questions that would be nice to address. It would be interesting to discuss 1/λ corrections.

One could also consider the exchange of a ﬁnite number of single-trace operators, combining the results of [149] with the methods of this note. Other interesting directions would be to combine the method presented in this note with recent direct computations of Witten diagrams at one loop [150] and with integrability based approaches [151].

accepted.question_text: Can conformal field theories on real projective space, including strongly coupled examples such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory, be solved well enough to compare their one-point and two-point data with holographic predictions for the same background?

evidence.quote: In the future, it would be interesting to study holographic models such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory and compare them with the holographic predictions.

accepted.question_text: Within the proposed theory of quasi Riemann surfaces associated with defects, can one explicitly construct local quasi-holomorphic curves, give a spacetime interpretation of the local gauge symmetry of the bundle of quasi Riemann surfaces, and determine whether restricting the defect fields to tiny defects produces genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?
accepted.context_brief: Quasi Riemann surfaces and defect QFT

evidence.quote: Explicit constructions of local quasi holomorphic curves are needed, say for M = S2n.
The local gauge symmetry in the bundle of quasi Riemann surfaces needs a space-time interpretation.
Tiny defects look like points in M, so ﬁelds Φ(ξ) when restricted to the small ξ in Q will give ordinary local quantum ﬁelds onM. Will these form new local qfts in 2n-dimensions?
